fullName: Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging beamline: station 9-ID-D and the 9-ID-GT 'Grand Tube'

status2026.detail: Operations at the old 9-ID, including USAXS and the Bionanoprobe, ended on 1 August 2022. Its enclosures were removed by 22 December 2022, according to the 9-ID home page and news. The Grand Tube arrived in four sections in August 2023 and was installed in September and October 2023. The source slide dates first light to run 2024-2, but this must refer to the source and front end. X-rays could not enter 9-ID-A before shielding verification on 18 December 2024. That day, verification covered 9-ID-A and the mini-hutch. Verification of 9-ID-D and the Grand Tube followed on 28 to 30 January 2025. Technical commissioning began on 3 February 2025, and full operations began on 14 March 2026. In run 2026-2, starting 27 May, 50% of beamtime was allocated through the Beamtime Allocation Committee. From run 2026-3, starting 9 September, 80% is allocated to General User Proposals for GI-SAXS/WAXS/XPCS and CSSI. The Beamline Directory lists 9-ID-D as 'Operational/Accepting General Users', with on-site access. Only the downstream undulator is installed. A liquid-surface diffractometer and multilayer monochromator from the 2019 design are absent from the installed-component lists.

tagline: Study the shape and motion of nanoscale structures on chips and thin films with X-rays at grazing angles.
summary: Thin films in chips and solar cells often lie on thick supports that obstruct measurements through the sample. At the Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging beamline, CSSI, coherent X-rays strike the surface at a fraction of a degree. Their waves have stable phase relationships, so X-rays scattered by different structures interfere in a grainy pattern called speckle. Scientists reconstruct 3D structures from this pattern and measure changes in films over times from a millisecond to many minutes. For imaging, each speckle must cover several detector pixels. The detectors are positioned up to 22 m from the sample inside the Grand Tube, a walk-in vacuum vessel about 20 m long. The beamline entered full operation in March 2026.

whatAPSUEnables.text: Surface speckle imaging requires coherent X-rays with stable phase relationships. Before the upgrade, about 0.05% of the APS beam at 10 keV was coherent. Recording one usable pattern from a large gold test object in 2012 took a few hours. The upgraded electron beam is about 12 to 15 µm wide horizontally, depending on mode, compared with about 275 µm before. These are root-mean-square widths. A few percent of the X-rays are now coherent, so measurements of realistic samples take less time. For photon-limited XPCS at fixed signal-to-noise ratio, acquisition time, contrast and pixel count, doubling the coherent flux permits four times shorter time intervals. A hundredfold flux increase could permit 10,000 times shorter intervals under those conditions, though the camera's millisecond frame time remains a practical limit. Source estimates give roughly 100 to 200 times more coherent flux. The 2017 projection of 100 to 1,000 assumed a longer source than the single 2.35 m undulator now installed.
quantitative: At 10 keV, the coherent fraction was about 0.05% before the upgrade, with σx = 275 µm and σy = 10 µm. For the 2.35 m revolver on APS-U, it is about 2.6% in round-beam mode or 6% in flat-beam mode. These estimates use the 2024 storage-ring source parameters and λ/4π per plane.

At 10 keV and 30 m from the source, the horizontal coherence length was about 2 µm before the upgrade. The APS-U estimates are about 48 µm in round-beam mode or 41 µm in flat-beam mode. The vertical values are about 58 µm before and 70 to 160 µm after. These estimates use ξ = λz/(2πΣ) and the 2024 storage-ring parameters.

The U21/U25 revolver peak brilliance exceeds 10²² ph/s/mm²/mrad²/0.1%BW at 10 keV. The 2017 Preliminary Design Report and the 9-ID source-characteristics slide describe a hundredfold increase over the old Undulator A. The slide gives about 2 × 10²² for the U21 first harmonic near 10 to 11 keV, compared with about 1.1 × 10²⁰ at the old APS U33 peak.
The 2017 Preliminary Design Report gives a coherent fraction of 0.01 to 0.1% across the hard X-ray range before the upgrade.

The 2012 CSSI demonstration at 8-ID-E used about 10⁹ coherent photons per second at 7.35 keV and a detector 0.7 m from the sample. Each pattern took a few hours and peaked at 3,000 counts. The resolution was 2.6 µm along the beam, 22 nm across the surface and 2.7 nm normal to the surface. Sources are the 2017 Preliminary Design Report and Sun et al., 2012.

FDR Table 4.58 gives design flux at 8.8 keV of 9.2 × 10¹³ ph/s/0.1%BW in a 0.75 × 0.42 µm spot with the KB mirrors, accepting 3 × 2 coherent modes. The CRL-2 value is 9.4 × 10¹³ in a 3.5 × 1.7 µm spot. The CRL-1 full-beam value is 3.4 × 10¹⁴ in a 29 × 16 µm spot. The Beamline Directory gives about 1.2 × 10¹³ photons per second for KB mode.

For photon-limited XPCS with fixed signal-to-noise ratio, acquisition time, contrast and pixel count, the shortest accessible time scales as 1/brilliance². A brilliance gain of about 100 would therefore permit about 10⁴ times shorter intervals. The squared scaling on the 9-ID source slide refers to this improvement factor. The stated GI-XPCS time range is 10⁻³ to 10³ s in the Beamline Directory and Strzalka, 2025.
The APS CSSI page gives sample-to-detector distances of 2.9 to 21.8 m in vacuum. The 2012 demonstration used 0.7 m, as documented in the 2017 Preliminary Design Report.

The 9-ID source slide gives coherent fractions of about 6% at 10 keV and 2% at 25 keV for APS-U U25/U21. The old APS U33 values are about 5 × 10⁻⁴ and 1.4 × 10⁻⁴. The gain read from the plot is about 100 to 150.

The 2017 Preliminary Design Report projected a coherent-flux increase of two to three orders of magnitude with 4.8 m of undulator. The installed device is 2.35 m long. Estimates for that source are about 100 to 200 times the old flux, using the design report, 9-ID source slide and 2026 APS insertion-device table.

techniques.name: Coherent surface scattering imaging
techniques.text: With coherent surface scattering imaging, CSSI, scientists reconstruct 3D surface structures without an imaging lens. X-rays strike the sample at about 0.1 to 1°, near the critical angle below which most incident X-rays are reflected. Scattered X-rays interfere in a speckle pattern. The measured pattern contains intensity, without the phase of each wave. Each speckle must cover at least two pixels so that software can recover the phases and reconstruct the object. This is called oversampling and phase retrieval. The scattering model includes reflections from the supporting substrate. In 2012, the resolution was 22 nm across the surface, 2.7 nm in height and 2.6 µm along the beam. Rotating the sample by a few degrees improves the along-beam information. Later work reached in-plane resolution below 5 nm.

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy
techniques.text: In grazing-incidence X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy, GI-XPCS, scientists measure changes in speckle intensity as structures near a surface move. Each region of the scattering pattern corresponds to a length scale. Software calculates how long intensity fluctuations remain correlated, expressed by the correlation function g₂. The dependence on length scale distinguishes diffusion, non-oscillating capillary waves on thick viscous films and steady ballistic rearrangement in jammed materials. With incidence below or above the critical angle, measurements sample the top few nanometres or the whole film. At 9-ID, measurements with the EIGER 16M camera, 3 to 20 m away in vacuum, cover times from a millisecond to 1,000 seconds.

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering
techniques.text: In grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering, GISAXS, scientists measure the average sizes, spacings and shapes of pores, grains or stripes across a film. X-rays strike at a shallow angle, and scattering through small angles corresponds to structures from about a nanometre to a few hundred nanometres. The result is an average over the illuminated area, rather than an image of an individual object. Analysis includes reflections from the substrate through the distorted-wave Born approximation. Measurements can continue during annealing, exposure to solvent vapour, spin coating or film growth. The EIGER 16M detector in the Grand Tube is used at long sample-to-detector distances.

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering
techniques.text: In grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering, GIWAXS, measurements at larger scattering angles give atomic and molecular spacings in thin films. Scientists also determine crystal orientation, called texture, which affects materials such as solar-cell films and plastic electronics. At 9-ID, up to 135 frames per second are recorded with a Pilatus 1M-F detector in air beside the diffractometer. Measurements can continue during heating or cooling on a Linkam stage, with a directory temperature range of about −180 to 300 °C, and during spin coating or electrochemical cycling. A robot arm is available for sample changes.

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence multibeam X-ray holography, Lloyd's mirror geometry
techniques.text: For grazing-incidence X-ray holography, the flat substrate is a reflecting surface, as in Lloyd's 19th-century experiment with visible light. X-rays scattered directly toward the detector interfere with X-rays scattered downward and reflected by the substrate. Scientists infer feature height from the spacing of the resulting fringes. The effect is strongest at exit angles below about 0.3°, away from the bright specular reflection. With detailed scattering simulations, 3D shapes can be reconstructed from one view with nanometre or sub-nanometre precision. Single-view measurements are useful for processes that cannot be repeated.

scienceCases.title: 3D measurements of surface nanocircuits
scienceCases.text: Chip makers need measurements of the widths and heights of patterned lines, called critical-dimension metrology. Cutting the chip destroys it, and transmission X-ray imaging of patterns on a thick wafer requires thinning the wafer. With CSSI and its holographic variant, scientists infer shape from grazing-angle scattering while the wafer remains intact. The 2012 demonstration used a gold 'Argonne' pattern and reached 22 nm resolution across the surface and about 2.7 nm in height. Later APS and PETRA III experiments reached better than 5 nm in-plane resolution. A semiconductor-metrology talk from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology, NIST, was included in the beamline's 2023 first-experiments workshop.

scienceCases.title: Single-view 3D measurements with Lloyd's mirror geometry
scienceCases.text: In Lloyd's mirror experiment, light interferes with its reflection. At grazing X-ray angles, interference between direct scattering and scattering reflected by a silicon substrate produces fringes related to surface-feature height. In 2023, Chu and colleagues reconstructed thicknesses of stacked gold bars on silicon from single views with nanometre or sub-nanometre precision. The data came from PETRA III and the pre-upgrade APS, with scattering simulated in more than 5 million cells. At 9-ID, this single-view method is intended for irreversible processes measured as they occur.

scienceCases.title: Reconstructing surface structures with scattering models
scienceCases.text: Standard lens-free reconstruction assumes each X-ray scatters once. Under that assumption, the diffraction amplitude is related to the object by a Fourier transform, and iterative algorithms recover the unmeasured phases. Near a reflecting surface, X-rays can also reflect between the substrate and structure, so this approximation fails. New algorithms simulate propagation through successive slices of a 3D model and adjust the model until calculated and measured speckle agree. Automatic differentiation supplies the changes needed to fit the model, using a method also used to train neural networks. A 2023 study reconstructed elongated 3D patterns from single frames in an 8-ID prototype experiment and simulations assuming a hundredfold source-flux increase. A 2026 framework specified sampling requirements and reconstructed isolated 3D objects from rotation series at one or two incidence angles.

scienceCases.title: Structural changes in polymer electronics
scienceCases.text: Polymers that conduct ions and electrons are used in biosensors. They swell and shrink as ions enter and leave. In a 2024 pre-upgrade experiment at 8-ID-I, a PEDOT:PSS film in a liquid cell was electrochemically doped and de-doped while GI-XPCS frames were recorded at ten per second. Scientists measured internal strain and slow structural rearrangement. The structure did not return directly to its initial state, a response called hysteresis, and continued changing slowly after switching back on. At 9-ID, GIWAXS measurements of molecular packing can accompany GI-XPCS measurements of dynamics over a millisecond to 1,000 seconds.

scienceCases.title: Crystallisation during solar-cell film spin coating
scienceCases.text: Perovskite solar-cell films crystallise while a solution of their ingredients is spun and dried. In 2022, GIWAXS measurements during 5-minute spin-coating runs identified two competing formation routes in mixed 2D/3D halide perovskites, which contain layered and bulk crystal forms. The routes were named the 'solvate' and 'orientation' mechanisms. Their relative contributions depended on the ingredient proportions, so scientists could adjust the film structure through composition. Those measurements used the 8-ID-E grazing-incidence instrument, now at 9-ID. The 2019 CSSI design lists 3D photovoltaic-film structure among six priority research areas. Spin coating, thermal and solvent-vapour annealing, and user solar simulators are supported at 9-ID.

scienceCases.title: Flow and structural change in thin films
scienceCases.text: Thermal capillary waves produce small height fluctuations on molten polymer films. Scientists measure their relaxation times with GI-XPCS. Experiments on ultrathin molten polystyrene in 2007 required an elastic term, a shear modulus, in the capillary-wave model, indicating partly solid-like behaviour. Coherent GISAXS measurements can also follow the development of ion-beam-induced surface ripples. In a 2021 NSLS-II study, the slowest relaxation occurred at length scales with the strongest structural correlations, an effect called de Gennes narrowing. Surface self-assembly, capillary instabilities in confined geometries and interface dynamics are among the research areas in the 2019 design.

scienceCases.title: X-ray measurements of mirror shape
scienceCases.text: The 9-ID focusing-mirror shape-error specifications are below 0.3 nm horizontally and 0.2 nm vertically, expressed as root-mean-square values. These limits restrict the increase in focal spot size to no more than 3% above the ideal. Testing optics with X-rays at their intended wavelength, called at-wavelength metrology, is a CSSI priority research area. A compact wavefront sensor designed by the APS optics group is installed just downstream of the CSSI sample station in 9-ID-D.

keyParameters.label: Energy range
keyParameters.value: 6–25 keV, fully tunable
keyParameters.note: The 2019 design range was 6 to 30 keV. The source slide gives continuous tuning from 8 to 25 keV. The U25 fundamental reaches about 4.6 to 5 keV, so the operating lower limit of 6 keV comes from the optics and operations.

keyParameters.label: Focal spot sizes
keyParameters.value: 0.6 × 0.35 µm to 3.5 × 1.7 µm (H × V) in coherent modes
keyParameters.note: At 8.8 keV, the 2019 design gives 0.75 × 0.42 µm with KB mirrors, 3.5 × 1.7 µm with CRL-2 and 29 × 16 µm with the full CRL-1 beam.

keyParameters.label: Sample-to-detector distance (in vacuum)
keyParameters.note: The APS feature page gives a working distance of 2.9 to 21.8 m without identifying the reference sample. This dossier assumes CSSI. Strzalka, 2025, gives 3 to 20 m for GISAXS and GI-XPCS. MEDSI, 2020, gives up to 23 m in the design, and SPIE, 2025, gives more than 20 m.

keyParameters.label: Grand Tube (9-ID-GT)
keyParameters.value: ~20.5 m long, 2.75 m diameter stainless-steel vacuum vessel with an 8 mm wall, rated for pink beam
keyParameters.note: Dimensions differ across sources. Structural Dynamics, 2025, gives 20 m × 2.75 m. The APS feature page gives 66 ft long and about 9 ft across. APS News, 2023, gives 70 ft and 100,000 lb. The 2023 APS-U news and September update give 20 m long and 3 m across. The 2020 shielding design study gives 20.5 m, 2.75 m and an 8 mm wall.

keyParameters.label: Detectors
keyParameters.value: In-vacuum EIGER 16M (400 fps, 550 fps burst); in-vacuum MM-PAD; in-air Pilatus 1M-F (135 fps)
keyParameters.note: EIGER 16M pixels are 75 µm, with about 18 megapixels. The PDR format of 4,150 × 4,371 pixels and 311 × 328 mm, at 133 Hz, describes the first-generation EIGER X 16M. The installed variant is unpublished, and the stated 400/550 frames per second exceeds that model's 133 Hz. MM-PAD pixels are 150 µm. Its mixed integration/counting operation permits a wide intensity range. The 2017 PDR gives 256 × 384 pixels and a 47 × 49 mm active area. These disagree, since the stated pixels imply 38.4 × 57.6 mm.

keyParameters.label: GI-XPCS time window
keyParameters.value: 10⁻³ to 10³ s
keyParameters.note: The same range is given in Strzalka 2025.

keyParameters.label: Source
keyParameters.value: One revolver undulator (U21 / U25 arrays, 2.35 m) in the downstream slot; upstream slot empty
keyParameters.note: The 2019 baseline included an upstream planar U21 and downstream revolver, as listed in FDR Chapter 3, Table 3.13.

keyParameters.label: U21 array (APS21#10)
keyParameters.value: 112 periods, Keff 1.38 and E1 8.34 keV at 8.5 mm gap; 5.4 kW, 216 kW/mrad² at 200 mA
keyParameters.note: User minimum gap 9.0 mm, where E1 is ~8.9 keV (estimated).

keyParameters.label: U25 array (APS25#8)
keyParameters.value: 94 periods, Keff 1.99 and E1 4.58 keV at 8.5 mm gap; 8.1 kW, 225 kW/mrad²

keyParameters.label: Electron source (ID straight, round-beam mode)
keyParameters.value: σx 12.3 µm, σy 8.26 µm, σx′ 2.34 µrad, σy′ 3.47 µrad (28.7 pm each plane)
keyParameters.note: Flat-beam mode: 14.5 / 3.08 µm and 2.75 / 1.29 µrad. Both sets are zero-current values.

keyParameters.label: Coherent fraction (derived)
keyParameters.value: ~2.6% (round) / ~6% (flat) at 10 keV; ~0.8% / ~2% at 25 keV
keyParameters.note: Derived here as (λ/4π)² / (Σx Σx′ Σy Σy′) for L = 2.35 m.

keyParameters.label: Front end
keyParameters.value: HHL front end, windowless (differential pump), 2 × 2 mm exit mask at 25.4 m
keyParameters.note: Limits of the high-heat-load front end: 21 kW and 590 kW/mrad².

keyParameters.label: Mirrors
keyParameters.value: Two horizontally deflecting mirrors in 9-ID-A: MR-1 flat, MR-2 bendable; stripes include Pt, Si and Cr
keyParameters.note: The 2019 design used one flat mirror at 2.4 mrad with Si/Pd/Pt stripes. The 2020 shielding study assumed two mirrors at angles of at least 3.0 mrad.

keyParameters.label: Monochromator
keyParameters.value: Horizontally deflecting LN2-cooled double-crystal monochromator (HDCM), fixed exit
keyParameters.note: Strzalka, 2025, describes horizontal double-crystal deflection. The FDR specifies liquid-nitrogen cooling, a fixed exit and Si(111) pseudo-channel-cut geometry. Its 4.65 × 1.08 mm horizontal-by-vertical footprint at 13.0° also implies horizontal deflection. The Beamline Directory high-resolution mode gives ΔE/E = 2.8 × 10⁻⁵, consistent with Si(311), but the installed crystal set is unconfirmed. The XBPM drawing places the monochromatic beam 10 mm outboard of the pink beam at 42.38 m.

keyParameters.note: The directory gives tunable focal spots of 0.5–30 µm (Beamline Directory).

MEDSI, 2020, gave 550 mm. The FDR placed Pt-coated vertical and horizontal mirrors 1,000 and 800 mm upstream of the sample at 2.5 mrad.

insertionDevices.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#5, U21 array APS21#10
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator with two magnet arrays on a rotating carriage
insertionDevices.notes: The U21 array has 112 periods. Its length, calculated as 112 × 21 mm, is 2.35 m. The source slide gives 2.3 m. The device minimum gap is 8.5 mm, the administrative minimum 8.72 mm and the user minimum 9.0 mm. At 8.5 mm, Keff is 1.38 and E1 is 8.34 keV. Total power is 5.4 kW and power density 216 kW/mrad² at 200 mA. The FDR flux calculations use an 8.8 keV fundamental and 26.4 keV third harmonic. The installed device is in the downstream slot, with its centre about 1.25 m downstream of the straight-section centre in the FDR. The 9-ID source slide describes a 2.3 m tandem revolver with 21 and 25 mm periods and continuous tuning from 8 to 25 keV. The 2026 APS insertion-device table defines effective periods as N − 2. At the 9.0 mm user minimum gap, the estimated fundamental is about 8.9 to 9.0 keV. The FDR's 8.8 keV U21 fundamental at K = 1.305 is therefore just below that range, but is accessible with U25.

insertionDevices.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#5, U25 array APS25#8
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator, second array in the same device
insertionDevices.notes: The U25 array has 94 periods. At 8.5 mm gap, Keff is 1.99, E1 is 4.58 keV, total power is 8.1 kW and power density is 225 kW/mrad². Staff rotate it into position in place of U21 for lower fundamental energies. With the first and third harmonics of both arrays, the energy range is 6 to 25 keV, or up to 30 keV in the 2017 PDR. The 9-ID source slide gives continuous tuning from 8 to 25 keV.

insertionDevices.name: Upstream slot, planned planar U21, uninstalled
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet undulator in the FDR baseline
insertionDevices.notes: The 2019 FDR, Table 3.13, specifies a dual-inline arrangement with an upstream planar U21, downstream U21/U25 revolver and phase shifter/corrector. Table 4.56 assumes both devices, with 4.6 m total length, for its flux estimates. The upstream position remains empty as of September 2026, according to the source slide and 2026 APS insertion-device table. It is reserved for a possible second undulator.

source.canting: There is no canting. One device is installed in the downstream slot of the dual-inline straight section. The beam follows the straight-section axis.
source.frontEnd: The APS-U High Heat Load Front End has power limits of 21 kW total and 590 kW/mrad². In beam order, it contains the permanent-magnet clearing magnet, LPPS, storage-ring valve, burn-through fixed mask BTFM1, FM2, collimator, GRID XBPM1, FM3, photon shutter PS2 with intensity monitor IM1, safety shutters SS1 and SS2, and the wall collimator through the ratchet wall. The exit table in 9-ID-A contains a 2 × 2 mm mask with XBPM2 at 25.4 m and a 5 × 5 mm tungsten collimator at 26.1 m. The 9-ID exit is windowless, with a built-in differential pump, as specified in FDR Chapter 3, Table 3.1 and Section 3-2.1, and Chapter 4, Section 4-8.3. Design power through the 2 × 2 mm mask is 2.10 kW for two U21 devices at K = 1.305 and 0.812 kW for U25 at K = 1.939, from FDR Table 4.56.
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: The August 2024 storage-ring parameters give zero-current electron-beam sizes and divergences at an insertion-device straight. Intrabeam scattering at 200 mA increases them somewhat. In round-beam mode, σx = 12.3 µm, σy = 8.26 µm, σx′ = 2.34 µrad and σy′ = 3.47 µrad, with 28.7 pm emittance in each plane. In flat-beam mode at κ = 0.1, horizontal and vertical sizes are 14.5 and 3.08 µm, and divergences are 2.75 and 1.29 µrad. For a 2.35 m undulator, the calculated single-electron photon terms are σr = √(2λL)/4π and σr′ = √(λ/2L). They are 1.9 µm and 5.1 µrad at 10 keV, and 1.2 µm and 3.2 µrad at 25 keV. With the photon terms included, the round-mode photon source at 10 keV is about 12.5 × 8.5 µm rms, with 5.6 × 6.2 µrad rms divergence. Photon divergence is the larger contribution. The 2017 PDR, Table 6.18, gave APS-U size ranges of 5 to 30 µm horizontally and 2 to 14 µm vertically, compared with 275 and 10 µm before the upgrade.

branches.name: 9-ID single line (pink or monochromatic)
branches.description: The beam follows one line without canting or branches. After the horizontally deflecting monochromator, the monochromatic path is about 10 mm outboard of the pink-beam path at 42.38 m, according to the XBPM drawing. Both paths pass through masks in 9-ID-A and 9-ID-MH, including the dual-aperture PM-5 and pink-beam stop BS-2. Three sample positions in 9-ID-D share the downstream Grand Tube detectors. They are the CSSI solid-sample station at 54.992 m, the GI-XPCS hexapod near 55.9 m and the GIXS diffractometer at 56.590 m.

components.name: Empty upstream undulator slot
components.distanceNote: The upstream position is estimated as the mirror image of the downstream device at +1.25 m in FDR Table 4.56. It is not explicitly given in a source. The 3D model depicts an empty outline.
components.text: The upstream slot is reserved for a second undulator. Two magnet arrays fit in sequence in the electron-ring straight section. The 2019 design included a planar undulator with a 21 mm period here, for 4.6 m of combined undulator length and greater brightness. As of September 2026, only the downstream slot is occupied. The manual describes space for a future second device.

components.name: Revolver undulator U21/U25 (APS21R25#5)
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.56: the revolver's centre is 1.25 m downstream of the centre of the straight section, the origin for all distances on this beamline.
components.text: X-rays are emitted as electrons pass between rows of alternating magnetic poles and change direction repeatedly. The radiation from successive bends interferes to produce an intense, narrow beam. This revolver undulator has two magnet arrays on a rotating mount, with 21 mm and 25 mm periods. Staff select the array for the desired photon energy and adjust the gap to tune it. The fundamental and third harmonic, at three times the fundamental energy, cover 6 to 25 keV. Peak brightness near 10 keV is about 100 times the old APS undulator value. The 2.35 m device has been this straight section's only undulator since 2024.

components.name: High-heat-load front end (windowless, in the tunnel)
components.distanceNote: The front end is estimated to extend from 14 to 23 m inside the tunnel. FDR Table 3.9 places the first beam-position monitor and upstream mask of APS-U front ends at 19.4 m. Internal positions for the 9-ID front end are unpublished.
components.text: The front end is inside the concrete shielding of the accelerator tunnel. The outer parts of the X-ray beam are absorbed in water-cooled masks, beam position is monitored, and the beam can be blocked by safety shutters. The standard APS-U high-heat-load design is rated for 21 kW. Vacuum sections are separated by pumping gas out in stages, called differential pumping. There is no exit window, which avoids distortion of the coherent beam as it passes through window material.

specs.main elements: clearing magnet, masks, GRID-XBPM, photon and safety shutters

components.name: Ratchet shield wall (with wall collimator)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated at 22.1 to 23.6 m by comparison with the 28-ID ray-trace plan used for CHEX. The 9-ID position is undocumented.
components.text: A thick concrete wall separates the accelerator tunnel from the experiment hall. X-rays pass through a small opening lined with a metal collimator that blocks radiation outside the beam path. The wall position, about 22 to 24 m from the source, is estimated from other APS sectors.

components.name: Front-end exit mask (2 × 2 mm, with XBPM2)
components.distanceNote: Position from FDR Table 4.57.
components.text: The front end ends at a water-cooled metal block with a 2 mm square opening. The central beam passes through, and the rest is absorbed as heat. An X-ray beam-position monitor, XBPM2, is integrated into the block. The vacuum sections downstream are separated by differential pumping without a beryllium window.

components.name: Front-end exit collimator (tungsten, 5 × 5 mm)
components.distanceNote: Position from FDR Table 4.57.
components.text: This tungsten block has a 5 mm square opening for the X-ray beam. Radiation outside that opening is absorbed. It blocks bremsstrahlung, the very-high-energy radiation emitted when ring electrons collide with residual gas atoms.

specs.aperture: 5 mm × 5 mm, narrowed for small-offset monochromators

components.name: Slits SL-1 (white beam, 9ID-SL-1)
components.distanceNote: Position from FDR Table 4.57, which specifies high-heat-load white-beam slits with tungsten edge inserts. The installed label is 'Slits, PB 9ID-SL-1'.
components.text: Four movable jaws with tungsten edges define a beam about a millimetre square for the first mirror. They are designed for high heat loads. At this point, the beam is still 'white', with the full range of energies emitted by the undulator.

specs.defines: Mirror acceptance about 1 × 1 mm. The FDR gives 0.96 × 1.0 mm².

components.name: Mirror MR-1 (flat, horizontal deflection; 9ID-MR-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: At the first mirror, useful X-rays are reflected sideways at a grazing angle of a few milliradians, a small fraction of a degree. Reflection occurs below an energy cutoff set by the angle and coating. The highest-energy X-rays continue along the original path. The mirror is flat, water-cooled and ultra-smooth. In the 2019 design, about two-thirds of the incident 474 W was absorbed. Platinum, silicon and chromium coating stripes are selected by translating the mirror. Beam deflections before the final focusing mirrors are horizontal, a common arrangement for stable coherent beams.

components.name: Secondary collimator SC-1 (9ID-SC-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m. The 2019 design position was 29.1 m.
components.text: A small aperture in a heavy-metal block is just downstream of the first mirror. Radiation scattered outside the aperture, including stray high-energy radiation from the storage ring, is absorbed in the block.

components.name: Beam flag BD-1 (diamond screen; 9ID-BD-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m. The 2019 design position was 29.5 m.
components.text: Staff lower a diamond screen into the beam to check its position and shape. The diamond glows where X-rays are absorbed. A camera records that image at about 16 µm per pixel. With the first mirror withdrawn, the measured image is of the direct undulator beam.

components.name: White-beam stop PM-1 (9ID-PM-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Unreflected X-rays are absorbed in a cooled stop on the original beam axis. The useful beam has already been reflected sideways at the first mirror. The stop is rated for the raw 'white' beam with its full range of energies.

components.name: Movable photon mask PM-2 ('DAMM'; 9ID-PM-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Selected parts of the beam are blocked at this movable photon mask to protect downstream equipment. It is labelled 'DAMM' on the installed-layout drawings, but the abbreviation is not publicly explained. The shielding study assumed a beam defined by a pinhole-like opening and two mirrors.

specs.tag: 9ID-PM-2 on the layout drawing. The manual list's 9ID-PM-1 appears to be a typo.

components.name: Secondary collimator SC-2 (9ID-SC-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Stray scattered radiation is absorbed in a heavy-metal collimator just before the second mirror.

components.name: Mirror MR-2 (bendable, horizontal deflection; 9ID-MR-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: At the second mirror, X-rays are reflected onto a path parallel to the original beam axis, with a small sideways offset. Bending the mirror adjusts beam convergence. It has the same coating stripes as the first mirror. A second reflection reduces unwanted high-energy radiation and removes a direct line of sight to the source. The shielding study assumed two mirrors at angles of at least 3.0 mrad for the Grand Tube to qualify as its own radiation enclosure. The 2019 design had one mirror. Installed angles are unpublished.

specs.coating stripes: Same four stripes as MR-1. Chromium was in use in the log.
specs.design basis: shielding study assumed two mirrors at ≥ 3.0 mrad

components.name: Photon mask PM-3 (9ID-PM-3)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Stray X-rays after the second mirror are absorbed at this cooled mask. It is rated for 'pink' beam, which has been filtered by the mirrors but still contains a range of photon energies.

components.name: Beam flag BD-2 (9ID-BD-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Staff lower a second diamond screen into the beam to check its position and shape after the two mirrors. Camera images are available for both the direct white beam and the mirror-filtered pink beam.

components.name: Photon mask PM-4 (9ID-PM-4)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Pink-beam radiation outside the mask opening is absorbed as heat before reaching the monochromator crystals. The mask protects the crystals from stray radiation.

components.name: Bremsstrahlung collimator BC-1 (9ID-BC-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: Bremsstrahlung outside the beam opening is absorbed in this dense collimator before the monochromator. This very-high-energy radiation originates in collisions between ring electrons and residual gas atoms. The collimator is part of the radiation-safety system.

components.name: Slits SL-2 (pink beam, 9ID-SL-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m. The 2019 design position was 29.9 m; it moved downstream when the second mirror was added.
components.text: The pink beam is trimmed to the required size at horizontal and vertical slits before the monochromator. Their position is downstream of the 2019 design location because a second mirror was added.

components.name: Monochromator HDCM (horizontal double-crystal, LN2-cooled; 9ID-MN-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m. The 2019 design position was 30.65 m.
components.text: A narrow band of X-ray energies is selected by two silicon crystals. At a chosen crystal angle, waves reflected from successive atomic planes interfere constructively at one wavelength, called Bragg diffraction. The 2019 design used 13.0° at 8.8 keV. Liquid-nitrogen cooling limits distortion from absorbed heat, about 160 W in that design. The fixed-exit arrangement maintains the outgoing beam position during energy changes. Deflection is horizontal, with the monochromatic beam about 10 mm beside the pink-beam path.

specs.flag inside: Diamond and CdWO₄ screen, tagged 'Flag3 9ID-BD-3'. The tag is also used for XBPM-1.

components.name: Dual-aperture mask PM-5 (9ID-PM-5)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-A layout in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 897. The scale is anchored to the 2019 design positions of SL-1 at 27.1 m and the downstream enclosure wall near 36.9 m.
components.text: The mask has openings for both the pink beam and the monochromatic beam, whose paths are about 10 mm apart after the monochromator. Radiation outside either opening is blocked. Either beam mode can be used downstream.

components.name: Shielded transport pipe (9-ID-A to 9-ID-MH)
components.distanceNote: The extent is estimated between the 9-ID-A wall near 36.9 m in FDR Fig. 4.51 and the mini-hutch near 41.5 m.
components.text: X-rays pass through a shielded vacuum pipe about 5 m long between the first optics enclosure and the mini-hutch. The pipe is supported on stands across the open hall floor, with shielding to contain scattered radiation.

components.name: Pink-beam stop BS-2 (with gate valve GV-5; 9ID-BS-2)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m.
components.text: The pink beam is absorbed at this stop at the mini-hutch entrance during monochromatic operation. Pink beam contains a range of energies after filtering at the mirrors. The monochromatic beam passes about 10 mm to one side of the stop. Adjacent gate valve GV-5 separates the vacuum sections when closed.

components.name: Beam-position monitor XBPM-1 (Sydor; 9ID-BD-3)
components.distanceNote: Exact: 42.380 m on the XBPM drawing; a survey on 3 December 2024 gave 42.4186 m.
components.text: Beam position is monitored here so staff can detect and correct drift. The pink and monochromatic paths are 10 mm apart. The monitor is centred between them and has up to 13 mm of sideways travel to measure either beam. A 22 mm opening is available for bypass. Its surveyed position is about 42.4 m from the source, one of the few published installed positions on this line.

components.name: Slits SL-3 (pink beam, 9ID-SL-3)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m.
components.text: Stray light around the beam is blocked at these slits before the first lens set. They are rated for pink-beam and monochromatic operation.

components.name: Photon shutter PH-1 (9ID-PH-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m.
components.text: The beam is blocked at this shutter inside the mini-hutch, upstream of the first lens set. Another shutter is at the hutch exit. The safety role of PH-1 is inferred from its name and position and is undocumented.

components.name: Transfocator CRL-1 (9 lens cartridges; 9ID-RL-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m.
components.text: The focal length depends on the selected combination of nine lens cartridges. X-rays change direction only slightly in each curved lens, so several lenses are stacked. The cartridges contain 1 to 8 lenses with apex radii from 2 mm to 0.1 mm. Beryllium is assumed as the lens material. With CRL-1 alone, the design focus is 29 × 16 µm for grazing-incidence scattering and XPCS. CRL-1 is also used for prefocusing before the downstream lenses and mirrors.

components.name: Beam flag BD-4 (9ID-BD-4)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m.
components.text: Beam images are recorded with a screen and camera after the first lens stage, with either pink or monochromatic X-rays.

components.name: Shutter SH-1 (9ID-SH-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the mini-hutch layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 898. The scale is anchored to the surveyed position of beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m. The 2019 design had a pink-beam shutter at 35.5 m.
components.text: The beam is blocked at this station shutter at the mini-hutch exit before entering the experiment station, 9-ID-D. The 2019 design listed a pink-beam shutter farther upstream.

components.name: Fast shutter (9ID-BI-8)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-D layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 895. The scale is anchored to beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m and the CSSI station at 54.992 m, from ELOG 916. The 2019 design had slits at 47.7 m.
components.text: The X-ray beam is blocked between camera exposures to limit dose to delicate films. Shutter timing is electronically synchronised with the detector.

specs.timing: Synchronized to detector exposures with softGlue

components.name: Attenuator AT-1 (filter foils; 9ID-AT-1)
components.distanceNote: The 2019 design placed filters at 48.2 m. The installed filters share the fast-shutter table, according to the 9-ID User Manual. The illustrated position is approximate.
components.text: Beam intensity is reduced in steps by inserting thin metal foils. The attenuator is used when intensity is too high for the sample or detector, in either pink-beam or monochromatic mode.

components.name: Slits SL-4 (9ID-SL-4)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-D layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 895. The scale is anchored to beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m and the CSSI station at 54.992 m, from ELOG 916.
components.text: These slits block stray radiation before the second lens set. A smaller opening selects a part of the beam with stable phase relationships across its width. The 2017 design specified about two vertical coherence lengths and three horizontal coherence lengths. A coherence length is the distance over which the phase relationship between waves remains correlated.

specs.planned opening (PDR): About two vertical and three horizontal coherence lengths

components.name: Transfocator CRL-2 (10 lens cartridges; 9ID-RL-2)
components.distanceNote: Position based on FDR Table 4.57. The installed order is SL-4, CRL-2 and SL-5, according to the 9-ID User Manual.
components.text: The second transfocator contains ten cartridges with 1 to 16 compound refractive lenses each. The 2019 design focus was 3.5 × 1.7 µm at 8.8 keV. The accepted beam contains about six coherent modes, each with stable phase relationships across it. Limiting the number of modes preserves speckle contrast.

components.name: Slits SL-5 (9ID-SL-5)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-D layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 895. The scale is anchored to beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m and the CSSI station at 54.992 m, from ELOG 916.
components.text: Stray radiation is blocked at the final slits before the focusing mirrors. These slits, like those upstream, are rated for pink beam.

components.name: Beam-position monitor XBPM-2 (Sydor; 9ID-BD-5)
components.distanceNote: Exact: 53.432 m on the XBPM drawing; a survey on 3 December 2024 gave 53.3988 m.
components.text: Beam position is monitored just before the focusing mirrors to check alignment. The surveyed position is 53.40 m from the source. Its lateral offset is nearly the same as the first monitor, 11 m upstream, indicating a beam path parallel to the original axis.

components.name: KB focusing mirrors (Kirkpatrick–Baez pair; 9ID-MR-3)
components.distanceNote: In the 2019 design, the vertical and horizontal KB mirrors are 1.0 and 0.8 m upstream of the sample at 55 m, at positions 54.0 and 54.2 m. The SPIE 2025 abstract gives about 650 mm working distance to the installed CSSI sample at 54.992 m. The illustrated mirror positions are approximate.
components.text: The final focus is formed at a Kirkpatrick–Baez pair of curved mirrors arranged at right angles. X-rays are focused vertically at the first mirror and horizontally at the second. The design target is a diffraction-limited spot about 500 nm across, at a working distance of about 650 mm beyond the last mirror. Diffraction is the spreading associated with wave propagation. Angular-stability requirements are 14 to 19 nanoradians, equivalent to a 1 cm coin viewed from 500 to 700 km. Mirror shape errors must remain below 0.3 nm. Both mirrors are mounted in ultra-high vacuum on the same granite table as the sample station, with laser-interferometer measurements of position.

specs.coating: Platinum in the FDR design. The installed coating is unpublished.
specs.working distance: About 650 mm in SPIE, 2025, and 550 mm in MEDSI, 2020
specs.figure error: Rms below 0.3 nm horizontal and 0.2 nm vertical
specs.mirror spacing: About 0.27 m, with the vertical mirror upstream

components.name: Window WN-1 (Be or SiN; 9ID-WN-1)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-D layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 895. The scale is anchored to beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m and the CSSI station at 54.992 m, from ELOG 916.
components.text: A thin beryllium or silicon-nitride window separates the ultra-high-vacuum focusing optics from the sample chamber, which operates at ordinary high vacuum. X-ray absorption in these materials is low.

components.name: CSSI sample station (solid samples, in vacuum; 9ID-BI-2)
components.distanceNote: The 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 916, gives the CSSI solid-sample station at 54,992 mm.
components.text: The solid sample is vertical inside a vacuum chamber, with X-rays incident at a fraction of a degree and scattering in a horizontal plane toward the Grand Tube. Positioning uses flexure stages, whose motion comes from elastic bending rather than sliding. Position is measured with laser interferometers. At 1° incidence, a 1 µm height change shifts the beam footprint by 57 µm along the surface. Surface-location accuracy must therefore be better than 50 nm, with angular stability of about 50 nanoradians. Rotation stages set the incidence angle and sample yaw for 3D measurements. The sample and focusing mirrors share a granite table to reduce relative motion.

specs.degrees of freedom: Five, comprising three linear axes, pitch and yaw
specs.angular stability: 50 nrad requirement in MEDSI, 2020, and 55 nrad in SPIE, 2025
specs.metrology: Three frames with capacitive sensors and laser interferometers

components.name: Wavefront sensor (9ID-BD-6)
components.distanceNote: Position estimated to ±1 m from the installed 9-ID-D layout and component list in the 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 895. The scale is anchored to beam-position monitor 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m and the CSSI station at 54.992 m, from ELOG 916. It is listed directly after the CSSI station.
components.text: The wavefront is measured here to check distortion introduced by the mirrors and lenses. A wavefront is a surface of equal X-ray phase. The compact sensor was designed by the APS optics group and is installed just after the CSSI sample station. Its measurement method is unpublished.

components.name: GI-XPCS hexapod (Aerotech HEX500-350HL)
components.distanceNote: The illustrated hexapod position is calculated from the instrument notes. It is downstream of the CSSI solid-sample station on the stationary granite of the GIXS table. The manual gives 1.552 m from the hexapod centre to KB-H and 1.818 m to KB-V. Assuming KB-H is about 0.65 m upstream of the sample at 54.992 m, the hexapod is near 55.9 m.
components.text: Heavy sample cells for GI-XPCS are supported on a six-leg hexapod. Platform position and tilt are adjusted by changing the leg lengths. GI-XPCS measures surface dynamics from speckle-intensity fluctuations. The platform is 500 mm across, and the high-load Aerotech model is the same as the rheometer hexapod at 8-ID-I. It arrived in October 2024.

components.name: GIXS diffractometer (GISAXS/GIWAXS, from 8-ID-E)
components.distanceNote: The 9-ID User Manual, ELOG 916, gives GIXS at 56,590 mm.
components.text: Thin films lie horizontally on this instrument, transferred from 8-ID-E. Measurements can continue during heating, cooling, solvent-vapour annealing, spin coating and deposition. A small robot arm is available for sample changes. Wide-angle scattering is recorded with a detector nearby in air. Small-angle scattering is recorded with the EIGER detector in the Grand Tube.

specs.temperature range: −180 to 300 °C in the directory. The manual gives −196 to 350 °C.

components.name: GIWAXS detector Pilatus 1M-F (on motion system 9ID-BI-7)
components.distanceNote: The illustrated position is approximate. The in-air detector is downstream of and beside the GIXS sample. Its position varies on the WAXS motion system, according to the 9-ID User Manual.
components.text: Wide-angle scattering from the film is recorded with a Pilatus 1M-F detector in air. From the pattern, scientists determine molecular spacings and crystal orientations. The detector has 172 µm pixels, a separate positioning system and a maximum frame rate of 135 frames per second.

components.name: Grand Tube (in-vacuum flight path, 9-ID-GT)
components.distanceNote: The vessel start is approximate. The APS CSSI page gives detector distances of 2.9 to 21.8 m from the sample, corresponding to source distances near 57.9 to 76.8 m. With about 20.5 m vessel length in Sunil, 2020, the estimated extent is 57.4 to 77.9 m. The 2019 flight path was 58.0 to 76.0 m. The 3D model places the vessel at 57.5 to 78.0 m.
components.text: The Grand Tube is a steel vacuum vessel about 20 m long and 2.75 m across. Speckle size increases with sample-to-detector distance, and each speckle must cover several pixels for reconstruction. Detectors are positioned on a carriage 2.9 to 21.8 m from the CSSI sample, with vertical and lateral movement as well. Vacuum limits unwanted X-ray scattering from air. The 8 mm stainless-steel wall is also the radiation shield, so the tube is a certified X-ray enclosure. It weighs about 45 tonnes and arrived in four sections in August 2023.

specs.length: About 20.5 m. Other sources give 20 m, 66 ft or 70 ft.

components.name: EIGER 16M detector (in vacuum, on the carriage)
components.distanceNote: The detector is movable near 57.9 to 76.8 m, or 2.9 to 21.8 m from the CSSI sample, according to the APS CSSI page. A source distance of 75.0 m is about 20 m from the sample. The illustrated carriage is 20 m from the sample, with the EIGER beside the MM-PAD. The arrangement is illustrative.
components.text: Individual X-ray photons are counted with an 18-megapixel detector inside the Grand Tube vacuum. At 20 m from a 0.75 µm sample spot and 8.8 keV, a speckle spans about 50 of its 75 µm pixels. The frame rate is 400 per second, or 550 in bursts. Carriage position determines speckle size, and lateral movement extends the range of recorded scattering angles. The EIGER 16M is used for CSSI, GISAXS and GI-XPCS.

specs.format: About 4150 × 4370 pixels, 311 × 328 mm. These PDR values describe the first-generation EIGER X 16M. The installed variant is unpublished.
specs.frame rate: 400 frames per second, with 550 in burst mode
specs.vacuum rule: powered off while pumping or venting between 1 bar and 0.01 mbar

components.name: MM-PAD detector (mixed-mode, in vacuum)
components.distanceNote: The detector is movable inside the Grand Tube. The exact mounting is unpublished. For illustration, the 3D model places it on the EIGER 16M carriage, 0.45 m upstream, centred on the specular-reflection spot.
components.text: The specular reflection and faint speckles are recorded together with the mixed-mode pixel array detector, MM-PAD, developed at Cornell. Near the critical angle, reflection can reach 10¹¹ counts per second per pixel. Useful speckles are 8 to 10 orders of magnitude weaker. Measurement of this intensity range combines charge integration and counting within each pixel. No beam stop is required in front of the detector, so the low-angle data needed for reconstruction are measured. The installed version is unpublished.

specs.format (PDR): 256 × 384 pixels. The PDR also gives 47 × 49 mm, inconsistent with the 38.4 × 57.6 mm implied by 150 µm pixels.
specs.peak rate it must handle: up to 10¹¹ counts/s per pixel near the critical angle
specs.vacuum interlock: Power is cut above a gauge reading of 10⁻³, since June 2026.

components.name: End-of-line beam stop
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.57 gives a pink-beam stop at 78.0 m. Its 8ID-BS-1 label appears to be a typo. The installed end stop is not publicly documented, and its illustrated position is approximate.
components.text: Any beam reaching the downstream end of the Grand Tube is absorbed in this final stop. It is rated for the full pink beam. The installed stop is not publicly documented.

enclosures.name: Storage-ring tunnel / front end
enclosures.role: source (revolver undulator, downstream slot) and HHL front end
enclosures.notes: Straight-section limits are approximate, with about 5.4 m straight length. The ratchet wall is estimated at 22.1 to 23.6 m by comparison with other APS-U sectors.

enclosures.name: 9-ID-A
enclosures.notes: Boundaries were read from the scale in FDR Fig. 4.51, with about ±0.3 m uncertainty. The enclosure is wedge-shaped in plan. It contains the front-end exit table, SL-1, MR-1, MR-2, masks, collimators, flags, SL-2, the HDCM and dual-aperture mask PM-5. Shielding was verified on 18 December 2024.

enclosures.name: Shielded transport
enclosures.role: shielded beam transport on the hall floor (9-ID-A to 9-ID-MH)
enclosures.notes: The transport extends from the 9-ID-A wall near 36.9 m in FDR Fig. 4.51 to the mini-hutch near 41.5 m. Support stands are about 2 m apart in the FDR plan.

enclosures.name: 9-ID-MH
enclosures.role: mini-hutch (pink-beam capable) for CRL-1, XBPM-1 and shutters
enclosures.notes: The mini-hutch was added after the FDR design, which had open transport from 37 to 47 m. Its extent is estimated around the surveyed XBPM at 42.38 m. It contains BS-2, BD-3, SL-3, PH-1, RL-1, BD-4 and SH-1. Shielding was verified on 18 December 2024.

enclosures.name: Shielded transport (MH–D)
enclosures.role: shielded beam transport on the hall floor (9-ID-MH to 9-ID-D)
enclosures.notes: This short transport connects the mini-hutch near 45 m to 9-ID-D near 47 m.

enclosures.name: 9-ID-D
enclosures.role: experimental station: beam conditioning, CSSI solid-sample station, GI-XPCS hexapod, GIXS diffractometer + WAXS detector
enclosures.notes: The upstream boundary is from FDR Fig. 4.51 and the PDR, which combined the old B, C and D stations into one station starting at 47 m. The downstream boundary is estimated where the Grand Tube begins. In photographs, the tube is outside the hutch. FDR Fig. 4.57 also calls this station 9-ID-B. Shielding was verified on 28 to 30 January 2025.

enclosures.name: 9-ID-GT (Grand Tube)
enclosures.role: self-shielding in-vacuum detector flight path (walk-in vacuum vessel) on the open experiment floor
enclosures.notes: The cylindrical vessel is 2.75 m in diameter and about 20.5 m long, with an 8 mm stainless-steel wall, domed end head and external stiffening rings. It is light grey in APS photographs. It contains the longitudinal detector carriage, EIGER 16M and MM-PAD. Shielding was verified on 28 to 30 January 2025.

instruments.name: CSSI solid-sample instrument (KB + solid sample station 9ID-BI-2)
instruments.text: The solid-sample instrument combines Kirkpatrick–Baez focusing mirrors with a high-vacuum sample station on granite air-bearing stages. A chip-like sample is mounted on edge about 650 mm downstream of the mirrors. Five groups of flexure stages provide coarse alignment and fine scanning. Position is measured with capacitive sensors and laser interferometers. The design targets are a 500 nm diffraction-limited spot, mirror-angle stability of 14 to 19 nanoradians and sample-angle stability of about 50 nanoradians. Installation took place in 2024 and 2025. Speckle patterns are recorded with the EIGER 16M and MM-PAD detectors in the Grand Tube.
sampleEnvironments: In-plane (yaw) rotation series for tomographic CSSI

instruments.name: GIXS instrument (GISAXS / GIWAXS), migrated from 8-ID-E
instruments.text: The grazing-incidence scattering instrument for horizontal thin films was moved from 8-ID-E. Wide-angle scattering, measured with an in-air Pilatus 1M-F beside the sample, gives information about molecular packing. Small-angle scattering, measured with the EIGER 16M at 3 to 20 m in the Grand Tube, gives information about nanoscale structure. Measurements can take place during heating, cooling, solvent-vapour annealing, spin coating or deposition. A robot arm changes samples. Automated software transfers the data to high-performance computers for analysis.

instruments.name: GI-XPCS setup (high-load hexapod + Grand Tube)
instruments.text: Researchers measure surface and buried-interface motion by recording thousands of speckle frames and calculating how quickly their intensities change. Samples are mounted on a high-load hexapod on stationary granite. The EIGER 16M is 3 to 20 m away in vacuum. Measured time intervals range from a millisecond to 1,000 seconds. Correlation software runs on graphics processors in automated workflows.

instruments.name: Grand Tube detector system (9-ID-GT)
instruments.text: The Grand Tube is a walk-in vacuum vessel about 20 m long, with a movable detector carriage. At greater sample-to-detector distances, speckles extend across more pixels. Phase retrieval requires this oversampling. At larger sideways or vertical offsets, the measured scattering angles are larger, corresponding to finer detail. Researchers combine measurements at several positions to cover more of the pattern. The 8 mm stainless-steel wall is rated as pink-beam shielding. Pressure interlocks switch off detector power or high voltage outside safe operating conditions.

geometryNotes:
CSSI has one non-canted insertion-device line. Only the downstream revolver is installed in the dual-inline straight section, with its source point about 1.25 m downstream of the section centre. All distances in this dossier use the straight-section centre as the origin, following the FDR tables.

The line is on the main experiment-hall floor. The first optics enclosure, 9-ID-A, extends from about 23.6 to 36.9 m and is wedge-shaped in the plan of FDR Fig. 4.51. Shielded transport connects it to the added mini-hutch, 9-ID-MH, at about 41.5 to 45 m. Another transport leads to 9-ID-D at about 47 to 57.5 m. The free-standing Grand Tube, 9-ID-GT, extends from about 57.5 to 78 m. Its pink-beam-rated stainless-steel wall is its radiation shield. The light-grey vessel is 2.75 m across, with about four flanged sections, stiffener rings, a dished downstream head and floor saddles. These features are documented in APS photographs and the CSSI page. The line ends near the outer hall wall, with about 90 m available.

All deflections before the KB mirrors are horizontal. Flat MR-1 and bendable MR-2 form an offset pair about 2.9 m apart in the layout. After the HDCM, the monochromatic path is about 10 mm outboard of the pink path at 42.4 m. PM-5 therefore has two apertures, and the beam-position monitor has a bypass. Surveyed XBPM bodies at 42.42 and 53.40 m have nearly the same lateral offsets from the white-beam axis, X = −8.79 and −8.64 mm. This indicates a parallel, laterally displaced beam downstream, as documented in the XBPM drawing.

At the KB pair, the first reflection is vertical and the second horizontal. The FDR gives a 2.5 mrad grazing angle for the vertical mirror, corresponding to about 5 mrad upward or downward deflection. The direction is undocumented. The focus is about 0.65 m downstream, and beam height is about 1.4 m above the floor throughout.

The installed order in 9-ID-D is documented in the user-manual isometric drawing. A fast shutter and attenuator are on the upstream optical table, followed by SL-4, CRL-2, SL-5 and the XBPM-2 table. Downstream are the KB ultra-high-vacuum chamber on granite, a window and the round multi-port CSSI sample chamber on granite. The hexapod is on stationary granite beyond the chamber. The GIXS diffractometer is on translating granite with the in-air Pilatus detector arm. The Grand Tube entrance flange is in the downstream wall.

CSSI sample surfaces are vertical, with incidence and specular reflection in the horizontal plane. GIXS sample surfaces are horizontal, with vertical exit angles in the usual GISAXS geometry. The detector carriage moves along z and in x and y inside the 2.75 m bore.

Published installed z positions are limited to CSSI at 54.992 m, GIXS at 56.590 m and the XBPMs at 42.38 and 53.43 m. Other positions are estimated to ±1 m. The inboard or outboard deflection directions of MR-1 and MR-2 are unpublished. Only the monochromatic-to-pink offset direction is documented.

The 3D model uses documented longitudinal distances. Mirror-pair offsets of about 17 mm, from two roughly 3 mrad reflections 2.9 m apart, and the HDCM offset of about 10 mm are too small to see at hall scale. The rendered beam therefore follows one axis. MR-1 and MR-2 are drawn with outboard deflection for illustration. The Grand Tube axis is drawn 0.2 m above beam height to clear the saddles. Its actual axis height is unpublished.

The illustrated CSSI incidence angle is 0.5°, with an inboard-facing sample surface whose real facing direction is undocumented. The 1° specular reflection reaches about 0.35 m inboard of the direct beam at 20 m distance, at the drawn MM-PAD position. The EIGER 16M is farther inboard at larger exit angles. In the magnified view above the sample chamber, sample size is increased eightfold and angles 24-fold.

interactiveIdeas.title: Grazing angle and penetration depth
interactiveIdeas.concept: Adjust a silicon wafer from 0 to 1° incidence. Plot reflectivity, penetration depth and the illuminated footprint. Below the critical angle, reflection is nearly total and the evanescent field extends only a few nanometres into the surface. Above it, penetration increases.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Relate depth sensitivity to incidence angle and explain the approximately 0.2 mm footprint of a 1 µm beam at grazing incidence.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: The critical angle is αc = sqrt(2δ), with δ proportional to λ²ρe. At 8.8 keV, αc is about 0.20°, or 3.5 mrad, for silicon and 0.50° for gold. It scales as 1/E. Below αc, penetration depth is about λ/(4π sqrt(αc² − α²)), typically a few nanometres. Include β for absorption. Footprint length is beam size/sin(α). A 0.75 µm beam at 0.2° gives about 215 µm. The Yoneda peak is at αf = αc.

interactiveIdeas.title: Detector distance and speckle sampling
interactiveIdeas.concept: Move the EIGER/MM-PAD along the tube from 2.9 to 21.8 m and sideways. Choose energies from 6 to 25 keV and spot sizes from 0.6 to 3.5 µm. Display the speckle pattern on a pixel grid, oversampling ratio and smallest resolvable feature.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Relate speckle sampling to detector distance, and relate finer resolved detail to larger scattering vectors obtained closer to the sample or off axis.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Speckle size is s ≈ λD/d, where d is the illuminated size projected normal to the exit direction. Oversampling is O = s/p, with O ≥ 2 per dimension required by Nyquist sampling and about 5 preferred. At 8.8 keV, D = 20 m and d = 0.75 µm give s ≈ 3.8 mm, or about 50 EIGER pixels. At 25 keV, d = 3.5 µm and D = 20 m give s ≈ 0.28 mm and O ≈ 1.9 for 150 µm MM-PAD pixels. Half-period resolution is about π/q_max, where q_max = (4π/λ) sin(theta_max). A detector half-width of 0.155 m at 20 m and 8.8 keV gives about 9 nm resolution. At 2.9 m, it is about 1.3 nm. Grazing-incidence resolution is poorer along the beam footprint. Rotation series reduce this anisotropy.

interactiveIdeas.title: Height measurements with Lloyd's mirror geometry
interactiveIdeas.concept: Move a nanoscale feature vertically above a reflecting substrate. Display the interference fringes near the detector horizon. Then provide a fringe pattern and ask the user to estimate feature height.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Infer height from interference between directly scattered X-rays and X-rays reflected by the substrate.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Include direct scattering and scattering reflected by the substrate. Near αf = 0, Fresnel reflectance approaches 1 and the reflection phase changes by about π. For feature height d, fringe period in qz is about 2π/(2d). Fringes are strongest for αf below about 0.3° and αi above αc, as in Chu et al., 2023. Include Fresnel reflectivity and absorption. This is dark-field scattering away from the specular reflection.

interactiveIdeas.title: Coherence before and after the upgrade
interactiveIdeas.concept: Place two virtual pinholes 30 m from the source, following Young's double-slit geometry. Switch between the 1996 to 2023 APS and APS-U source parameters and change photon energy. Display fringe visibility and the number of coherent modes, with particular attention to the horizontal direction.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Explain coherence and the source-parameter changes that made CSSI practical.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: The rms transverse coherence length is ξ = λz/(2πΣ), where Σ = sqrt(σe² + σr²) and σr = sqrt(2λL)/(4π). At 10 keV and 30 m, the round-mode APS-U horizontal length is about 48 µm, compared with about 2 µm for the old APS. Vertical values are about 70 and 58 µm. The coherent fraction per plane is (λ/4π)/(ΣΣ′). At 10 keV, the total is about 2.6% in round mode and 6% in flat mode, compared with 0.05% before the upgrade. Use the zero-current 2024 storage-ring parameters. The 2019 FDR brightness mode is a historical design. The 9-ID source slide gives about 6% coherent fraction at 10 keV and 2% at 25 keV for APS-U, consistent with the flat-beam calculation. The plotted old-APS value is about 0.05%. Display coherent flux, proportional to brilliance × (λ/2)², as the quantity that increased about 100-fold.

interactiveIdeas.title: Speckle correlation and relaxation time
interactiveIdeas.concept: Choose temperature, viscosity and thickness for a polymer-film speckle simulation. Select a detector pixel and display its intensity trace and calculated g₂ correlation.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Relate XPCS correlation decay to relaxation time and distinguish the scattering-vector dependence of diffusion and capillary waves.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use g₂(q,τ) = 1 + β|f(q,τ)|² and f = exp(−Γτ) for simple relaxation. For diffusion, Γ = Dq². For overdamped capillary waves on thick films, Γ = γq/(2η). For thin films, Γ ≈ γh³q⁴/(3η). Speckle contrast β is below 1 and depends on coherence and pixel-to-speckle size ratio. The shortest time interval is limited by detector frame rate, about 2 ms at 400 to 550 frames per second, and photon statistics. SNR ≈ βI sqrt(TτN). At fixed signal-to-noise ratio, acquisition time, contrast and pixel count, the shortest τ scales as 1/brilliance². The 9-ID time range is 10⁻³ to 10³ s.

interactiveIdeas.title: Transfocator settings and focal spot size
interactiveIdeas.concept: Select the nine CRL-1 and ten CRL-2 lens cartridges, with radii from 2,000 to 100 µm, and the KB mirrors. Display spot sizes from about 30 to 0.5 µm, photon flux and accepted coherent modes.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Explain weak X-ray refraction, stacked lenses and the relation between focal spot size and coherent flux.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: For parabolic lenses, thin-lens focal length is f = R/(2Nδ). For beryllium at 8.8 keV, δ ≈ 4.4 × 10⁻⁶, so N = 1 and R = 100 µm give f ≈ 11 m. Add inverse focal lengths for lens stacks. Use the imaging equation 1/p + 1/q = 1/f. Source size multiplied by magnification is convolved with diffraction, approximately λ/(2NA), to estimate spot size. Use the installed cassettes from the CRL design review. The FDR 12-stack lists describe an earlier design.

funFacts: The Grand Tube weighs about 100,000 lb, or 45 t. It arrived at Argonne in four crated sections in August 2023. Assembly took three weeks, and installation at 9-ID took place in September and October 2023.
The focusing-mirror angular-stability requirements are 14 to 19 nanoradians in MEDSI, 2020, and SPIE, 2025. For comparison, a 1 cm coin at about 500 to 700 km subtends that angle.

Near the critical angle, the specular reflection can reach the incident-beam intensity and 10¹¹ counts per second per pixel. Useful speckles are 8 to 10 orders of magnitude weaker. Both are measured with the mixed-mode detector, MM-PAD, without the usual beam stop.
The Grand Tube is about 2.75 m, or 9 ft, across and about 20 m long. Staff can walk inside it after completing the formal access procedure.
The 8 mm stainless-steel wall is also the radiation shield. The tube itself is the certified X-ray enclosure, 9-ID-GT, rather than a pipe inside a separate hutch.

In the 2012 demonstration at APS 8-ID-E, about 0.13% of scattered photons were detected with a CCD 0.7 m from the sample. One pattern took a few hours and peaked at 3,000 counts. The gold 'Argonne' test pattern was 400 µm long, 5 µm wide and 40 nm thick.
At 1° incidence, a 1 µm sample-height increase moves the beam footprint about 57 µm along the surface. The required surface-location accuracy is better than 50 nm.

At 10 keV and 30 m from the source, the horizontal coherence length is estimated at about 40 to 50 µm after the upgrade, compared with about 2 µm before. These estimates use the 2024 storage-ring parameters.
The former 9-ID USAXS instrument is now at 12-ID-E, and the Bionanoprobe is now at 2-ID-D. The GIXS instrument was transferred to 9-ID from 8-ID-E.
The holographic geometry follows Humphrey Lloyd's 19th-century mirror-interference experiment, with hard X-rays and a reflecting silicon wafer.

openQuestions: Installed longitudinal positions are public for the CSSI station at 54.992 m, GIXS at 56.590 m and the XBPMs at 42.38 and 53.43 m. The '09-ID Beamline Component Reference Table' and optics schematic are on access-restricted Box. All other positions here are FDR values or estimates from isometric drawings, with about ±1 m uncertainty.

The 9-ID-MH boundaries near 41.5 and 45 m and the 9-ID-D/Grand Tube interface near 57.5 m are estimated. Hutch widths are unpublished. The FDR plan figure appears to have different horizontal and vertical scales.

Installed mirror incidence angles are unpublished. The FDR specifies one M1 mirror at 2.4 mrad, while the shielding analysis assumes two mirrors at angles of at least 3.0 mrad. The fourth stripe material and the inboard or outboard direction of reflection at MR-1 are unknown.

The installed HDCM crystal set and fixed-exit offset are unconfirmed. The FDR specifies Si(111), and the PDR also includes Si(220). The directory's high-resolution bandwidth, ΔE/E = 2.8 × 10⁻⁵, is consistent with Si(311). The FDR states a 2 mm offset, but the XBPM drawing gives about 10 mm pink-to-monochromatic beam separation at 42.4 m. No double multilayer monochromator is in the installed lists, although one was reserved in both design reports.

CRL-1 was moved from 32.4 m in the first optics enclosure in the FDR to about 43 m in the mini-hutch. The installed CRL-1 and CRL-2 have 9 and 10 cassettes, all two-dimensional, with R ≥ 100 µm. The FDR specified 12 stacks, including one-dimensional lenses and R = 50 µm. The Beamline Directory still gives the FDR focal sizes of 29 × 16 µm and 3.5 × 1.7 µm. Installed spot sizes and fluxes therefore need confirmation.

Directory fluxes differ from FDR Table 4.58 by roughly a bandwidth factor or a factor of ten. At 8.8 keV, the directory gives 3.4 × 10¹³ photons per second with CRL-1, 9.4 × 10¹² with CRL-2 and 1.2 × 10¹³ with KB mirrors. At 25 keV, listed values include 3.2 × 10¹¹ and 3.7 × 10¹¹ photons per second, and a CRL-2 spot size of 3 × 12 µm. These values are indicative.

KB working distances differ across sources. In the FDR, the vertical and horizontal mirrors are 1.0 and 0.8 m upstream of the sample. MEDSI, 2020, gives 550 mm, and the verified SPIE 2025 abstract gives about 650 mm. The latter is the most recent value. The full SPIE paper with measured stability was inaccessible. Its abstract gives a 55 nrad sample-stability requirement, compared with 50 nrad in 2020.

Grand Tube dimensions differ across sources. Structural Dynamics, 2025, gives 20 m × 2.75 m, and the shielding paper gives 20.5 m × 2.75 m. The feature page gives 66 ft long and about 9 ft across, APS News gives 70 ft long, and the 2023 update gives 20 m × 3 m. The overall vessel length including the heads is probably about 21 m. The assumed inner diameter is 2.75 m.

The EIGER 16M variant, MM-PAD version, detector mounting and travel ranges are unpublished. The stated 400/550 frames per second suggests EIGER2 XE rather than X, but this is unconfirmed. The beam-stop arrangement for GISAXS and CSSI is undocumented.
